chapterTitle: English Unit 5: Parts of Speech, Pronouns & Punctuation (Order of Adjectives, Pronoun Case & Mechanics)
subject: english

questions.question: Teachers are always known for their passion for work.

options.A: Common noun
options.D: Abstract noun

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) Abstract noun. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: There was enough space in the apartment.

options.A: Adjective of Quantity
options.D: Demonstrative Adjective

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Adjective of Quantity. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the third-person restricted point of view to focus on the thoughts of the character?

options.A: "She glanced around the room, unsure of where to go next."
options.B: "They whispered to each other, but their words were lost in the noise."
options.C: "The sky darkened as the storm approached."
options.D: "The crowd grew restless, waiting for the announcement."

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) "She glanced around the room, unsure of where to go next.". This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: In which of the following sentences is the hyphen used incorrectly?

options.A: She has a well-developed sense of humor.
options.D: She has a high school diploma.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) She has a high school diploma.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the apostrophe?

options.A: The boys' are playing football.
options.D: The boys's room is clean.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) The boys' room is clean.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly uses inverted commas?

options.A: "I can't believe it's already over," she said.
options.B: "I can't believe it's already over" she said.
options.C: I can't believe it's already over" she said.
options.D: "I can't believe it's already over," she said.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) "I can't believe it's already over," she said.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Identify the correct use of the comma:

options.A: I went to the store, and bought some bread.
options.B: I went to the store and, bought some bread.
options.C: I went to the store and bought some bread.
options.D: I went to the store and bought, some bread.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) I went to the store and bought some bread.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct punctuation with a compound adjective?

options.A: She is a long-term employee at the company.
options.B: She is a long term employee at the company.
options.C: She is a long term-employee at the company.
options.D: She is a long-term employee at the company.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) She is a long-term employee at the company.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly places the apostrophe in the possessive form?

options.A: The teacher's book is on the desk.
options.B: The teachers book is on the desk.
options.C: The teachers' book is on the desk.
options.D: The teachers books is on the desk.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) The teacher's book is on the desk.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct comma usage.

options.A: The book was, interesting and thought-provoking.
options.B: The book was interesting, and thought-provoking.
options.C: The book was interesting and, thought-provoking.
options.D: The book was interesting and thought-provoking.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) The book was interesting and thought-provoking.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses inverted commas correctly?

options.A: "I need your help," she said.
options.C: I need your help," she said.
options.D: I need your help she said.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) "I need your help," she said.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: In the sentence, "After she arrived, the meeting began," the pronoun "she" is an example of:

options.A: Anaphora
options.D: Adjunct

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Cataphora. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: "Reading helps me relax _____ a long day."

options.A: Into
options.D: After

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) After. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences carries the correct order of adjectives?

options.A: She was wearing beautiful new red shoes
options.B: She was wearing red beautiful new shoes
options.C: She was wearing beautiful red new shoes
options.D: She was wearing new beautiful red shoes

questions.explanation: According to the conventional order of adjectives, Opinion ('beautiful') precedes Age ('new'), which precedes Color ('red'): 'She was wearing beautiful new red shoes.'

questions.question: It took a long time to discover the Atlantic. Choose the suitable group of articles:

options.A: The
options.D: The, A

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) The, An. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Rashid and Aliyan sent e-mails to each other over the summer. Which type of pronoun is used in the given sentence?

options.A: Demonstrative pronoun
options.D: Distributive pronoun

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Reciprocal pronoun. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: English is the language of the people of England. Choose the suitable group of articles:

options.A: An
options.D: The

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) The. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: You may receive anything that you like. The underlined word is:

options.A: Relative pronoun
options.D: Demonstrative pronoun

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Relative pronoun. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?

options.A: I have a test tomorrow; so, I must study tonight.
options.B: I have a test tomorrow; I must study tonight.
options.C: I have a test tomorrow; and I must study tonight.
options.D: I have a test tomorrow,; I must study tonight.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) I have a test tomorrow; I must study tonight.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence with inverted commas:

options.A: I asked, "Can you help me with this task?"
options.B: I asked, "Can you help me with this task"?
options.C: I asked "Can you help me with this task?"
options.D: I asked, Can you help me with this task?

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) I asked, "Can you help me with this task?". This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following uses the hyphen correctly?

options.A: She is a well known author.
options.D: She is a well known, author.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) She is a well-known author.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses commas correctly to separate items in a list:

options.A: I bought, apples oranges, bananas, and pears.
options.B: I bought apples, oranges, bananas and pears.
options.C: I bought apples oranges, bananas pears, and.
options.D: I bought apples, oranges, bananas, and pears.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) I bought apples, oranges, bananas, and pears.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inverted commas to indicate a direct quote?

options.A: She said "I'll be there soon",.
options.D: She said "I'll be there soon."

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) She said, "I'll be there soon.". This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly with a semicolon?

options.A: I can't go today; however I will try tomorrow.
options.B: I can't go today, however; I will try tomorrow.
options.C: I can't go today, however, I will try tomorrow.
options.D: I can't go today; however, I will try tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) I can't go today; however, I will try tomorrow.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence with commas and quotation marks:

options.A: "It's raining" she said "but, I don't mind."
options.B: "It's raining," she said, "but I don't mind."
options.C: "It's raining," she said "but I don't mind."
options.D: "It's raining" she said, "but I don't mind."

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) "It's raining," she said, "but I don't mind.". This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the hyphen correctly to join two adjectives?

options.A: He is a good looking guy.
options.D: He is a good looking, guy.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) He is a good-looking guy.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: They are going to announce the results tomorrow.

options.A: The results are going to be announced tomorrow.
options.C: The results have been going to be announced tomorrow.
options.D: The results are being announced tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) The results are going to be announced tomorrow.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Identify the type of the underlined pronoun: "Each of the players gave his best."

options.A: Possessive
options.D: Reciprocal

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Distributive. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Choose the correct article for the blank: He is ____ honest man.

options.A: a
options.D: no article

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) an. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.

questions.question: Choose the abstract noun.

options.A: Woman
options.D: Money

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Hate. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Parts of Speech and Punctuation Mechanics.
